requiredFindings.location: docs/implementation/m2/live-guards-x4/PROPOSAL.md:378-391, :400, :502-518 and :629-633 (I1 initialization, unwind source, X4-F3 scope and placeholder withdrawal)
requiredFindings.problem: I1's claimed initial state is not established by the cited first-read path. StopOnUnwind also latches an otherwise successful read made while the thread is already unwinding. At the lease-free point it still uses the bare StopObserver; LeaseFree.first_read can return Ok after that destructor has latched the gate, and OperationGuard.start then installs cause=None. The post-creation stop-transition rule cannot repair that initial LATCHED-without-cause state, because later transitions record only if they set LATCHED. With the placeholder withdrawn, a supported unwind latch can now become GuardRefusal::Invariant and lose its existing OBSERVER.FAIL_STOP/observer-fail-stop semantics.

evidence.detail: The source expressly documents successful reads from destructors during unrelated unwinding. StopOnUnwind::drop tests thread::panicking(), independent of the method's Ok outcome, and runs before read_sampled_with returns.

first_read accepts (Ok(value), _) without checking the gate after monitor return. start creates Shared.cause as None and spawns the observer without checking the incoming gate or carrying a pre-creation cause.

The production handoff carries the successful LeaseFree value into OperationGuard.start. No intervening gate-state check prevents the latched value from reaching guard creation. A FirstRead::Monitor(AlreadyStopped) already maps to the existing Live(FailStop { subject: latched }) row at :1085-1088.

The total transition rule begins only after guard creation and W-9 expressly permits lease-free bare latches. I1's base case assumes every successful first read is unlatched, and a missing cause is then treated as an impossible invariant breach.

counterexample: During unrelated unwinding, a destructor starts a native writer operation and its lease-free first read completes successfully; no rule in the law excludes this entry.
The monitor's success body sees Preparing and builds Ok(value). StopOnUnwind drops while thread::panicking() is true and performs the permitted bare LATCHED fetch_or.
LeaseFree.first_read returns Ok(value). The handoff can create a state-2 guard with cause=None.
An observer tick returns AlreadyStopped. Under the old code latched() stores FailStop(latched); under round 2's pure reader it returns Invariant and records nothing.

A later checkpoint/refusal cannot fill the slot: its transition sees LATCHED already set, so the iff-first-set record rule forbids insertion. The changed row can be the invariant row and finish can see None -> operation-stopped instead of the old recorded observer-fail-stop.
requiredFindings.fix: Establish the lease-free-to-guard boundary explicitly in this law and X4-F3's scope. A successful first-read result must not promote a gate latched by its unwind finalizer into a cause-less guard. Either refuse that latched first read/handoff through the existing fail-stop(latched) path before guard creation, or carry the correctly recorded pre-creation first cause into the guard under a fully specified transition rule. Preserve the conservative StopOnUnwind behavior, the existing failure vocabulary and reason, monitor history, and never-reset; do not clear the latch, classify it as CertainRefusal, or authorize an invariant-row exception. Extend source 4 and controls to cover a successful monitor return during unrelated unwinding, especially at the lease-free first read, and prove I1 at the actual guard entry.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The protocol avoids waiting for the monitor mutex while latching, and adds no cause-lock wait to successful admission. The stop transition still acquires the cause mutex, so its acquisition can contend. The inherited LD8-2 wording that the observer latch never waits and W-10's unqualified completes without waiting are broader than this protocol proves.
evidence: S11.6:365 requires every stop transition to acquire Shared.cause.
S11.6:412-414 permits cause acquisition alone or after the monitor lock and leaves successful admission free of cause locking.
W-10:508 exercises completion while the monitor is held; it does not establish uncontended cause acquisition or a native scheduling bound.
nonBlockingObservations.fix: Qualify these statements as no wait for the monitor mutex, no I/O or wait while holding the cause lock, and no added cause-lock wait on successful admission. Keep native scheduling qualification excluded.

questions.result: Prior RF and NB closed; new RF remains
questions.reason: For guards that satisfy I1 at entry, CertainRefusal and Stale(row) are recorded with their first latch. Observer ticks only read; AlreadyStopped and pre-/post-window OutsideWindow record nothing. Successful BeforeAdmission/AfterAdmission record Operator. LD8-9 provides the acceptance/integration dependency requested in round 1.

The nine source classes cover every post-creation latch site in og/rv/cs, including the checkpoint trailing closure, monitor poisoning and StopOnUnwind. FC is inductively sound once I1 holds: only the mutex owner sets LATCHED and inserts iff its prior bit was clear. However the claimed lease-free base case is false for a successful read during unrelated unwinding. The source table should describe all StopOnUnwind triggers rather than only a panic inside the method.

questions.reason: CertainRefusal maps to the existing operation-stopped reason. The unlatched finish path still uses None -> OperationStopped; recording CertainRefusal neither changes the latched predicate nor makes revoked true. questions.result: PASS conditional on the required entry repair
questions.reason: With valid I1, a latched reader can only find the first cause after taking the mutex, so it must never insert a placeholder. Returning Invariant without recording is suitable for a genuinely broken invariant, but the current bare lease-free unwind path is not such an impossible caller. FailStop(latched) remains the correct stated cause for post-creation unwind and poisoned-monitor sources.

questions.result: PASS for lock order and admission; NB-X4R8-R2-1 applies
questions.reason: The watcher/certain-refusal/stale transitions can take cause alone; monitor-side transitions take monitor then cause. No cause->monitor acquisition is introduced. The cause lock is taken only after callbacks return/unwind, never over observation I/O or a crash hold. Successful admission has no cause-lock acquisition; refusal readers may wait. Monitoring history, bracketing, cadence and stop conservatism must remain. The normal failure's supplied subject must be determined outside the critical section.
